subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a militarized cyberpunk truck as a single TypeScript module, with around 150 parts covering wheels on rigid joints, cab, cargo bed with a missile turret, neon glow effects, and SVG textures for paint details.

Now I'm defining the vehicle's dimensions and joint hierarchy: a ~7m long hull with chassis root, six wheels across three axles, a turret joint for the gun, and a box-geometry helper function for building the chassis parts. Each wheel gets a tire, rim, neon ring, and hub, positioned so the tires touch the ground at y=0.

Working out the hull's armor plating and cab geometry: lower body box from y 1.0–1.7, cab box from y 1.7–2.7, hood section at the front, and a slanted windshield plane connecting the hood top to the cab roof.

Still placing cab geometry...

I'm importing the clockwork kit for metal/panelled textures and glow, then defining custom paint patterns for camo, hazard stripes, and other surface treatments. For the rear, I'm adding an armored cargo container with a turret ring, missile pod tubes with glowing tips, and a turret body joint mounted on the hull.

Now I'm adding more details: twin rail gun barrels with glowing muzzle rings, a radar dish on a mast, antenna rods with red glow tips, side skirts, exhaust stacks, headlight boxes, a roof light bar, a front ram plow wedge, tow cables, neon underglow strips in cyan/magenta, a license plate decal reading "2077", and side emblem/text decals like "UNIT-77" plus fuel tanks and spare armor plates.

Working out wheel arch geometry now -- adjusting body width and wheel offset so the fenders clear the wheels without clipping, placing dark box fenders above each wheel and resizing the hull's vertical span to fit cleanly between them.

Spacing out the axle positions front to back so the three wheel pairs don't overlap, then setting the cab and bed depths to align with the body width before writing the hull joint helper function.

Writing part and wheel helper functions...

I'm sketching out the SVG textures needed: a neon emblem for the door and a gradient windshield with HUD-style reflection details.

Still planning texture ideas... I'm adding a plate decal reading "NX-2077," a stenciled unit label for the bed side, and a radar-style screen glow, plus rim textures for the wheel hubs mounted as planes on the wheel bones so they spin naturally.

Now I'm sketching positions for the side window planes on the cab, figuring out dimensions and placement relative to the slanted cab profile, and thinking about whether the camo paint should get an additional panel overlay on top.

For the rear bed, I'm sizing an armored container box behind the cab, leaving a gap for exhaust stacks and spine equipment, and placing a turret ring plus considering missile pod mounts along the bed sides.

Working out pod rotation geometry...

Laying out a 2×3 grid of six missile tubes on the pod, each a short cylinder protruding slightly from the box with a glowing tip cone, then moving on to define the turret joint and its base ring in world coordinates above the hull.

Now I'm shaping the turret shell as an extruded side-view profile for a chamfered body, attaching a gun joint on top, and positioning twin barrel cylinders symmetrically along the z-axis.

I'm checking barrel clearance over the cab roof, adding a muzzle brake and glow ring at the barrel tips, a shroud box around the barrel base, a sensor pod with a glowing red lens eye, an ammo box on the turret side, and starting on a radar mast.

Writing dish lathe profile...

I'm also planning an antenna array with thin glowing-tipped rods, a roof light bar with red/blue glow, a searchlight, sensors, and cab details like a roof armor plate and mirror arms.

Now I'm working out the door lines, grille with glowing slits, cyan-white headlight boxes, and a front ram bumper with hazard stripes and a wedge plow extruded from a cross-section profile.

I'm also planning underglow neon strips along the body flanks in cyan and magenta near the ram and wheel arches to give the vehicle a lit-up aesthetic.

For the lower chassis details, I'm positioning cylindrical fuel tanks between the front and rear wheels, checking the clearance against wheel edges so they don't clip, with one side getting a tank and the other a toolbox for asymmetry.

Now for the rear end: a bumper box, glowing red tail light strips, license plate, a tow hitch cylinder, rear armor panels, and twin vertical exhaust stacks. For the sides, I'm adding rib loops along the bed panels and placing decal planes for unit markings and door emblems, being careful to keep them clear of the window and cab geometry.

Skipping the hood gun idea, I'll add a roll-cage over the bed, a front winch cylinder, and axle/suspension details like shocks, differential spheres, and leaf springs. For colors, I'm planning a dark navy camo base with olive-grey patches and bright magenta, cyan, amber, and red accents over dark metal tones.

For the wheels, I'm keeping flat colors simple and using paint patterns like stripes or scales to fake tread texture on the tire cylinders, staying within the 64-color limit.

For the tire assembly itself, I'm layering a dark inner sidewall cylinder, a metal steel rim cylinder sized to peek slightly past the tire edge, and a thin glowing cyan torus ring positioned on the outer face, with a decal plane for rim detail -- then I'll add hub bolts next.

I'm sketching the rim SVG with a ring, five spokes, and hub lugs, and planning to set glow strength 0.6 on the window-type parts. For wheel placement, I'll loop over left/right sides and three z-positions, naming each joint uniquely and attaching tire/rim parts to those bones, then move on to roof details and a cable conduit swept between cab and bed using a catmull curve.

I'm adding hose sweeps along each side from bed to cab, plus an antenna array made of rods with glowing tip spheres, then writing the actual builder code using the established API—parts, glow imports from the glow kit, metal/panelled helpers from the clockwork kit, and SVG utilities—finishing with a camo patch pattern definition for the paint job.

Now I'm tuning the camo texture: adjusting the gap and panel sizing, bumping the paint resolution to 2048 for better texel density across the large painted hull area, and deciding to only apply the expensive paint material to the hull, cab, container, ram, tires, and turret while using plain color strings elsewhere to limit painted surface growth. I'm sizing and positioning the hull body box and figuring out how the cab extrusion should sit relative to it.

Next I'm positioning the container box behind the cab, then working out the cab's cross-section profile as a sequence of (z,y) points to form the sloped hood and windshield shape, and computing the windshield plane's position and surface normal from the slope between two of those profile points.

Now I'm placing the side window plane within the cab profile, sizing the roof plate and light bar on top, and leaving a gap at the rear of the cab for where the container will attach.

Adding exhaust stacks with glowing orange cap rings, amber hood vent slats, and a front grille with glowing cyan slits.

Now adding glowing white headlight boxes, resizing the grille to avoid overlapping with the headlights, and starting on the front bumper's ram-wedge shape.

Now placing the fenders over each wheel with side plates, then adding small mudflap boxes behind the rear wheels for detail.

Checking fuel tank placement against wheel clearances confirms no overlap, and the fender zones only affect wheel areas so that's fine too. Now I'm positioning the rear bumper box and tail light glow strip relative to the hull and container geometry.

Working through the plate position relative to the bumper height, then planning additions like a roll cage arch at the container's rear top, searchlights, and container side ribs spaced along the z-axis.

Now I'm detailing more exterior elements: armor rail boxes with hazard stripes, roof hatch plates, decal placements for unit markings and screens, and vent grills. Then I'm shifting focus upward to the turret assembly, positioning its base cylinder on the container roof, setting up the yaw rotation bone, and defining the gun joint position before working out the turret's shell outline coordinates.

Still placing turret details...

I'm checking the pod box clips through the container bottom and adjusting the base height up to about 3.05 to keep it clear, while nudging the mount box and pod x-offsets to roughly ±0.8.

Now I'm checking the turret ring position against the pods to confirm there's no overlap there, then moving to the radar mast placement — it conflicts with the pods at x ±0.8, so I'm shifting it toward z 0.1 with x around ±0.85, between the cab and turret shell, to keep everything clear of the barrels.

Placing the radar mast at x -0.8, z -0.1, tilted dish up at height 0.7, and mirroring an antenna array on the opposite side with tall rods. I'm also deciding to keep the write-up around 350 lines, add the emblem texture to the turret side and container rear, confirm the hose sweep function needs a radius parameter, verify the wheel joint rotation is fine with no rigid roles needed, and note the windows should get a glowing texture.

Now I'm designing the SVG textures: a HUD-style glass panel with gradient, light streaks, cyan lines and "TGT LOCK" text; a hexagonal magenta emblem with "77"; a convoy unit label in amber monospace (skipping kanji since fonts aren't available); and a license plate with "NX-2077" and "NEO CITY" text.

Now I'm sketching the wheel rim with spokes, lugs, and center cap, plus a dashboard-style screen texture with a glowing cyan graph. Moving into the actual Three.js build code, I'm setting up helper functions for boxes and cylinders that construct geometry with configurable color, position, bone, and rotation options.
